title: Let athena close --allow-legacy-usage excuse recovered legacy token mism
summary: The 2fsa invocation record's tokens disagree with its modelUsage; the gate rule already checks tokens, but the legacy scope only excuses records byte-identical in the parent commit. I assume this record is still only in the state directory, so `close` adds it as a new file and it is not excused. The change extends the flag, and only the flag, to such recovered records, still printing each one.

defaults_applied.how: Regression tests in the lifecycle and gate crates; cargo test and clippy must pass.
Criteria run the close with and without the flag and check the refusal and the printed record.
The fix covers the class of recovered legacy records, not only the one 2fsa record.
The limit on the excuse is enforced in the gate scope and tested.
The decision record and changelog are written for an outside reader.
One focused change to the legacy scope.
An independent verifier runs the tests.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Goal: the maintainer can close job 20261015-131540-2fsa with the flag, while new records stay strictly gated. Audience: the maintainer and the verifier, who run cargo test.

Read from crates/athena-gate/src/reconcile.rs and crates/athena-core/src/manage.rs: check_invocation covers the token comparison, and check_tree_excusing_committed excuses only invocation records byte-identical in the parent.
Inference, not run: in recover_interrupted, records read from the state directory become new files in the closing commit, so the legacy scope refuses them.
Without the flag the gate is unchanged. Outcome totals are still reconciled in full, and the closing outcome is summed from the records' models_used.
The verifier cannot run the real close, so a regression test with the 6/3136/275219/3821 vs 90/52656/3634696/134508 shape stands in for it.
question: Is the 2fsa invocation record already committed, or does it exist only in the state directory? I assumed the state directory.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new lifecycle test creates an interrupted job whose state-directory invocation record has measured tokens that disagree with its models_used (token counts, not just cost). `athena close --allow-legacy-usage` succeeds, prints a 'letting a legacy usage record through' line naming the token mismatch, and the closing outcome reconciles. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test lifecycle`.
The same close without the flag is still refused with 'usage records reconcile', and the message names --allow-legacy-usage. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test lifecycle`.

A gate test shows that, under the legacy scope, an invocation record that is new or altered outside `athena close`'s own recovery still fails reconciliation, and a wrong outcome total is still refused. Run `cargo test -p athena-gate`.
`cargo test` passes and `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.

docs/decisions.md has a new decision, or an amendment to D101, with the case, alternatives and the limit of the excuse. CHANGELOG.md and the close row in docs/design/athena-v0.md describe the wider coverage.
The flag's help text and doc comments in main.rs and manage.rs state exactly which records it excuses.

out_of_scope: Rewriting or deleting the 2fsa invocation record, since records are append-only.
Fixing the original usage bug that produced the token mismatch, unless it is found in the same code path.
Loosening outcome-total reconciliation or the strict gate for commits that do not use the flag.
The firstmate study request that job 2fsa was running.
departures: The cause of the refusal is inferred from reading, not reproduced, so the reading and verification forecasts are slightly lower and cost slightly higher than the reference.
